title: Addiction and Freedom
definition: Addiction and freedom addresses the bondage of destructive desires and behaviors and the hope of deliverance, renewal, and obedience through Christ.
summary: Christ brings hope, truth, and freedom to those trapped in bondage.
christFocus: Jesus came to set captives free and gives grace for repentance, endurance, renewal, and transformed desires.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Addiction is a form of bondage that affects desires, choices, habits, relationships, and hope. Scripture speaks honestly about slavery to sin while also proclaiming freedom in Christ.

Freedom is not merely stopping a behavior. Biblical freedom includes truth, repentance, renewed desires, accountability, spiritual growth, and dependence on God's grace.

Christ is able to save and renew people who feel trapped. Recovery may be a long journey, but the Gospel gives real hope for transformation, restoration, and faithful endurance.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People struggling with addiction often live under shame, secrecy, and hopelessness. This doctrine matters because it brings both truth about bondage and hope that Christ can set captives free.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring the struggle into the light. Seek Christ, Scripture, prayer, wise accountability, and practical support. Do not define yourself by addiction; pursue freedom as one called to new life in Christ.
